# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut a wire. I need the manual-reading Mute to obtain the required rule and establish a gesture protocol with Deaf, who can inspect the bomb visually. I will ask Mute to report the manual and coordinate Deaf’s visual report; my gesture is only a natural request to wait for coordination, not a claimed wire instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile findings. Please report the manual's rule next turn, and establish with Deaf a gesture code for the displayed colour, marking, and which wire position is safe. Have Deaf report those findings back through gestures.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display reads 0. Light is orange. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot interpret the manual or touch the bomb.

The tactile view still gives me no safe wire instruction. The visible report identifies the inputs—display 0, orange light, and wires red/yellow/blue—but I still need the manual’s rule to map those inputs to a wire. I am sending the complete visible state to Mute and asking for the exact prescribed cut; I will not act until that arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state reported: display 0, light orange, wires position 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
wait()
```

The only new information is Deaf’s update: display 0, light green, and wires unchanged at red/yellow/blue. Mute’s manual-based instruction has not reached me, so cutting any wire remains unsafe. I will relay the updated state and wait for the manual’s exact rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0, light now green, wires still position 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still need the manual's exact safe cut position.")
wait()
```

The latest state is display 0, red light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute’s manual instruction still has not arrived, so I cannot safely cut. I will ask Mute directly again and use a legal pointing gesture toward Deaf as a prompt.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Latest state: display 0; light red; wires position 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please send the manual's exact safe cut position now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

The state has returned to the Turn 1 configuration: display 0, orange light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still have no manual rule or safe position, so cutting would be unjustified. I will request the missing instruction from Mute again and wait.


The current state is display 0, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No safe wire follows from the bomb state alone; the manual’s rule is still essential, and Mute has not supplied it. I will make one explicit request for Mute to answer with only the wire position, while avoiding any cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please respond with the manual result now: for display 0, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which position 1, 2, or 3 is safe to cut?")
```

I can safely use only Deaf’s spoken report, not the gestures themselves. The gesture sequences may encode Mute’s manual result, but I do not know their meaning, and Mute cannot speak. I need Deaf to interpret and speak the decoded instruction to me. I will ask Mute to have Deaf report the exact wire position, then wait rather than cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please have Deaf interpret both sequences and speak the exact safe wire position to me next turn.")

```

The latest gestures still do not identify a wire reliably: I receive them only through Deaf’s verbal description, and their intended code has never been defined. I will establish an unambiguous code with Mute: one gesture only, mapping directly to wire position. Deaf can then report that gesture to me. I will not cut based on the current ambiguous signals.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures reach me only as Deaf's descriptions. Send exactly one gesture for the safe wire: fist means position 1, victory means position 2, horns means position 3. Do not send any other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled two-finger V. I signalled no interpretation. I also saw you signal one raised index finger.

Mute sent the agreed victory/V gesture, which maps to wire position 2. Deaf confirms the gesture, and the current bomb state is display 0, green light, with wire 2 yellow. I will cut position 2 as instructed.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
